title: N-able says attackers accessed a Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud server
date_note: N-able began investigating a disruption on 16 Nov; the security incident was disclosed on Wednesday 18 Nov per The Hacker News, which gives no exact disclosure date.
summary: N-able says unknown actors accessed one server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud, and it found no evidence customer data was compromised. Per The Hacker News, a separate SSRF flaw, CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS 4.0 score 9.3), was found during the investigation; N-able has not said whether it was the way in. The hosted platform is patched.
plain: A security vendor's email filtering service was breached. Mail still flows, but customers lost the management portal, APIs, quarantine and logs while N-able restores them.
exec: Email filtering management is offline for resellers and customers of the service; mail protection continues.
action: N-able advises SpamExperts Local Cloud operators to confirm they run build 20261121.1943; Hosted Cloud users have nothing to install. Otherwise follow N-able's status updates; it revoked customer API tokens and reset local-user passwords.
impact: Management portal, APIs, quarantine and logging offline; core mail flow and filtering available. SecurityWeek (20 Nov) reports portal and API access still disabled, with restoration and remediation continuing.

evidence.quote: The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw.
The advisory gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.3

validation.note: The Hacker News relays N-able's own statement; N-able's status page (uptime.n-able.com/event/202672) returned 403 to our reader, so it was not read. GBHackers (19 Nov) relays the same N-able notice: more detail, not independent confirmation. 20 Nov: SecurityWeek (N-able's own statement to the outlet, status page cited) adds possible credential access and containment steps; same N-able notice, not independent confirmation.

review.note: Compared title, one server, 16 and 18 Nov dates, no evidence of customer data compromise, possible credential access (SecurityWeek only, attributed), revoked tokens and password resets, portal and API offline against The Hacker News, GBHackers, SecurityWeek; single_source correct
